source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines GANMs on a supplied collection of vector groups and states that, under its conditional Condition 1 for every parent--node--nondescendant triple and causal minimality, the group DAG is identifiable from the joint distribution.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2022 and 2025, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Condition 19 gives the scalar differential obstruction; Definition 27 imposes it on conditional parent--node triples; Theorem 28 identifies the DAG of a causally minimal restricted ANM.
A reverse scalar ANM implies the displayed differential equation, and when both input and noise densities are Gaussian a reverse model implies that the mechanism is linear.

The paper identifies scalar-node DAG ANMs through a conditional-variance condition involving error variances and parent influence, and supplies a DAG structure-learning algorithm; it is not a prescribed-pair conditional-covariance-variation orientation result.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1207.1977v1 corresponding to the ICANN 2012 paper
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The model takes a collection of already grouped vectors and estimates a causal order among those groups in a linear model.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Causal Inference 12 (2024) published version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper states that it has operated under a fixed partition and calls learning partition--graph pairs under appropriate optimality constraints an interesting but challenging future problem.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Multivariate Analysis 112 (2012) published article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article proves uniqueness of irreducible linear independent-subspace factorizations up to trivial indeterminacies under finite covariance; it does not address nonlinear causal block mechanisms.
